key_insight: The paper shows that closing the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is impossible under common similarity assumptions, and requires a stronger combination of assumptions to recover near-homogeneous time complexity.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this means algorithm design cannot rely on weak similarity between workers’ data alone; stronger structural conditions are needed to justify fast asynchronous training on heterogeneous devices.
method: Prove impossibility results under first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms.
Test the interpolation regime and show weak interpolation is still insufficient.
Introduce strong interpolation plus local PL condition to derive a new time complexity bound matching homogeneous-setting worker-time dependence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results and proofs of optimal time complexity bounds; no experimental data or empirical evaluation is described.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on strong interpolation and local Polyak–Łojasiewicz conditions, so its practical applicability may be limited when real worker data are highly non-identical or non-convex.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
